# Emergency procedures

The safety pilot's word ends any discussion. Anybody may call "abort"; only the safety pilot flies.

## What the aircraft does by itself

From the flight controller's baseline (`platform/fcu/argus_2027.param`), which the preflight holds the aircraft to:

| What happens | When | The aircraft | Set by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Fence breached | outside the polygon or above 120 m | returns to the takeoff point (RTL), or lands | `FENCE_TYPE, FENCE_ACTION` |
| Battery low | under 21 V (3.50 V a cell) for 10 s | returns to the takeoff point (RTL) | `BATT_LOW_VOLT, BATT_FS_LOW_ACT` |
| Battery critical | under 19.8 V (3.30 V a cell) for 10 s | lands where it is | `BATT_CRT_VOLT, BATT_FS_CRT_ACT` |
| Transmitter lost | the throttle channel under 975, or no signal | returns to the takeoff point (RTL) | `FS_THR_ENABLE` |
| Ground station lost | no heartbeat from it for 5 s | returns to the takeoff point (RTL); not while a person is flying it in LOITER, ALT_HOLD, STABILIZE or another pilot mode | `FS_GCS_ENABLE, FS_OPTIONS` |
| Position estimate lost (EKF) | variance over 0.8 | lands where it is | `FS_EKF_ACTION` |

No failsafe lets the payload or the bucket go (`FS_OPTIONS` bit 5 is clear): what is carried comes down with the aircraft.

The mission stack adds its own:

- **A mission that fails** ends by the failure policy its sequence gives it, as in 2026: `abort_and_rtl` (the default: the executor asks for its abort mode, the parameter `abort_rtl_mode`, RTL as shipped) or `continue_to_next` (the sequence goes on to its next mission; the shipped drop and delivery sequences use it). The recovery names its own abort mode: RTL while the gripper has never closed and there is a position to fly home on; a landing from the first close on, and whenever there is no pose, no GPS fix or GPS is not trusted.
- **A takeover** (behind the flag `takeover_latch`): a flight mode the stack did not ask for stops the executor for good. It sends nothing and asks for nothing until a person re-arms it (`ros2 service call /mission_executor/rearm_autonomy std_srvs/srv/Trigger`) with the aircraft back in GUIDED.
- **The actuation lock** (behind the flag `actuation_lock`): the gripper and the drop servo answer only to a release state (DROP_PAYLOAD, GROUND_DWELL, ENGAGE, SET_DOWN) whose gates hold.

## What the people do

| Situation | Safety pilot | Operator | Spotter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The aircraft does something nobody expects | Switches to LOITER and flies it; lands when in doubt | Says "takeover" and sends nothing. With `takeover_latch` on the executor is out by itself; with it off (the 2026 behaviour) the operator stops the launch with Ctrl-C on the safety pilot's word | Keeps eyes on the aircraft, calls its position |
| It heads for the boundary | Lets the fence act; takes over if it has not by the line | Reads the mode aloud | Calls the distance to the line |
| Fence breached (the aircraft returns to the takeoff point (RTL), or lands) | Watches it do that; takes over only if it does not | Does not send a mode | Keeps its path clear |
| Ground station lost (the aircraft returns to the takeoff point (RTL); not while a person is flying it in LOITER, ALT_HOLD, STABILIZE or another pilot mode) | Watches it do that; if already flying it by hand, keeps flying and lands | Does not restart anything in the air | Calls the aircraft's position |
| Transmitter lost (the aircraft returns to the takeoff point (RTL)) | Says "no link"; cannot take over until it is back | Reads the mode aloud | Keeps its path and the landing spot clear |
| Battery low (the aircraft returns to the takeoff point (RTL)) or critical (it lands where it is) | Lets it; clears the landing spot by voice | Notes the time and the voltage | Clears people from under it |
| Position estimate lost (the aircraft lands where it is) | Takes over in a mode with no position hold (ALT_HOLD or STABILIZE) and lands | Says what the ground station shows | Calls drift and height |
| A person or a vehicle enters the flight area | Holds, then lands away from them | Calls "abort" | Shouts the warning, points |
| Payload or bucket hung up, swinging | Lands where it is, slowly | Does not command a release | Calls the swing |
| Crash | Disarms (throttle down, or the transmitter's kill switch) | Stops the launch (Ctrl-C), unplugs nothing yet | Keeps everyone back until props stop; a damaged battery is handled as a fire risk |
| Battery fire or smoke | Disarms | Calls the organisers' safety officer | Extinguisher or sand; nobody breathes the smoke |

After any of these: nothing is flown again until the lead has read the attempt's report (`tools/post_flight.py`) and said so.

## Taking over, and giving back

- Any mode switch on the transmitter takes the aircraft from the stack. With `takeover_latch` on, the executor then stays out.
- To give it back: the aircraft steady in GUIDED, the operator re-arms the executor on the safety pilot's word. The interrupted mission is not resumed: it ends by its failure policy. With `abort_and_rtl` the aircraft comes home (or lands, where the mission has named a landing); with `continue_to_next` the executor flies the sequence's next mission. Read the sequence's `failure_policy` before re-arming. When in doubt, do not re-arm: the safety pilot lands it.
- The 2027 missions keep the points they command 5 m inside the flight boundary when the sequence gives one; the June 2026 missions (every flag off, the profile `comp_2026`) have no such limit. The flight controller's fence acts either way, with its own margin of 2 m.
